title: Rabbi Chasida
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a disciple of Rabbi Hezekiah, as in the Yerushalmi, end of Maaser Sheni, and Sotah ch. 9, halakhah 1, where he asked Rabbi Hezekiah; and in Nedarim ch. 5, halakhah 5, Rabbi Shovetai and Rabbi Chasida brought a question before Rabbi Yose.

But as for what we find in the Yerushalmi in several places, Rabbi Chisdai and Rabbi Chisdayi, Hyman has already explained in the entry Rav Chisda that this is Rav Chisda of Babylonia. And in the Zohar, Bo 38b, it is stated that Rav Chisda lived in Kapitkai and times were hard for him, and afterward he lived among the 'masters of shields' in Sepphoris and merited much good. It is possible that this refers to this Rabbi Chasida, since Rav Chisda was a Babylonian and lived in Babylonia.

notes.text: Chasida is distinct from Chisda. “Masters of shields” is the literal idiom for eminent scholars; Hyman’s possible identification of the Zohar figure with this Chasida remains tentative.

Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 5:5 directly names Rabbi Shovetai and Rabbi Chasida bringing a case before Rabbi Yose. The same passage later has Mana asking Chizkiyah; this alone does not establish every teacher relationship in Hyman’s notice. Chasida remains distinct from Chisda, and Hyman’s possible Zohar identification and place-name interpretation remain tentative.
